newsitem.title: USA: AT&Ts Ron Ponder may be next to leave - report.
newsitem.headline: AT&Ts Ron Ponder may be next to leave - report.

text.p: Ron Ponder, the executive in charge of AT&T Corp's information technology operations, could become the latest senior official at the company to leave, the online edition of InformationWeek said on Friday.
Ponder is facing heavy pressure to cut costs in his department, where new AT&T President John Walter wants many operations outsourced, according to InformationWeek.

The trade magazine said in its online edition posted Friday that Ponder was resisting such a move because he thought it would undo much of the restructuring he implemented since joining the company as chief information officer in 1993.
AT&T spokeswoman Adele Ambrose said the company did not comment on "rumors about our executives," but confirmed that the company was seeking to cut costs in Ponder's division.
Ambrose said Ponder was heading the effort, which she said includes possibly outsourcing certain functions.

"He is in fact leading a team studying a range of options for lowering the cost and improving the performance of our information technology operations," Ambrose said. "Ron is leading that effort, and we're not going to comment beyond that."

Industry analyst Jeff Kagan said talk of Ponder leaving the company had been floating around since late February, shortly after AT&T announced a staff reorganization that included cutting several hundred jobs.

"He's a key player in helping the company to position itself from a plain, old phone company into an information and communications provider," Kagan said. "He's one of the icons. It would be a blow to the morale of the company, but as when Nacchio left, it would not be insurmountable."
Ponder's departure would follow those of other top AT&T executives, including that of Joseph Nacchio, who resigned in December as executive vice president of the consumer and small-business division.
Most recently the company's chief financial officer, Richard Miller, announced he would leave at the end of March.
